name: Senso-ji Temple
description: Tokyo's oldest and most famous Buddhist temple, founded in 645 AD. The massive Kaminarimon gate and Nakamise shopping street leading to the temple are iconic.
tips: Visit at dawn for empty photos and a magical atmosphere. The Nakamise shops open around 9-10am.

name: Meiji Shrine
description: Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, set within a 170-acre forested park that feels miles from the city. The towering torii gate at the entrance is Japan's largest wooden torii.
tips: Combine with a walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku afterward. Weekend mornings sometimes have traditional wedding processions.

name: Tokyo Tower
description: Built in 1958 and inspired by the Eiffel Tower, this 333m red-and-white lattice tower remains a beloved symbol of Tokyo. The views are especially beautiful at night.
tips: Best photographed from Shiba Park or Zojoji Temple at dusk when it lights up. The top deck requires a timed ticket.

name: Tokyo Skytree
admissionCost: ~¥2100 Tembo Deck (350m), ~¥3400 combo with Tembo Gallery (450m)
description: At 634m, this is the tallest structure in Japan and the tallest tower in the world. The observation decks offer sweeping views of Tokyo and on clear days, Mt. Fuji.
tips: Book tickets online to skip lines. Sunset visits are ideal for day-to-night transition views. The Solamachi mall at the base has great shopping.

name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
description: The only publicly accessible part of the Imperial Palace grounds, featuring beautiful Japanese gardens, old castle ruins, and seasonal flowers. A peaceful oasis in central Tokyo.
tips: Enter through Otemon Gate. The Ninomaru Garden is the highlight. Closed Mondays and Fridays.

name: Shibuya Crossing
nameJa: 渋谷スクランブル交差点
description: The world's busiest pedestrian intersection where up to 3,000 people cross at once during peak times. An absolute sensory overload of neon, crowds, and energy.
tips: Best viewed from above at Shibuya Sky, the Starbucks on the 2nd floor of Tsutaya, or Mag's Park rooftop. Most dramatic at night with all the neon.

name: Tsukiji Outer Market
description: The remaining outer market of the former Tsukiji fish market, packed with hundreds of food stalls, restaurants, and kitchen supply shops. A paradise for street food grazing.
tips: Go early and hungry. Try tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), fresh sushi, and grilled seafood on sticks. Most shops are cash only.

name: Toyosu Fish Market
hours: Tuna auction viewing from 5:30; market restaurants from ~5:00-15:00. Closed Sun/Wed/holidays.
description: The world's largest wholesale fish market, successor to Tsukiji's inner market. The tuna auction is legendary and the sushi restaurants here serve some of Tokyo's freshest fish.
tips: Tuna auction viewing requires advance online reservation (limited spots). The market restaurants have long queues - arrive before opening.

name: Hachiko Statue
description: Bronze statue honoring the loyal Akita dog who waited at Shibuya Station for his deceased owner every day for nearly 10 years. Tokyo's most famous meeting spot.
tips: It's tiny and always surrounded by tourists taking photos. Quick stop before or after Shibuya Crossing.

name: Rainbow Bridge & Odaiba
nameJa: レインボーブリッジ・お台場
description: A futuristic waterfront entertainment island connected to the city by the iconic Rainbow Bridge. Features a replica Statue of Liberty, beaches, and malls.
tips: Take the Yurikamome monorail for great bridge views. The area is best at sunset/night when the bridge lights up. TeamLab Planets is nearby in Toyosu.

name: Shibuya
description: The epicenter of Tokyo's youth culture with the famous scramble crossing, towering video screens, and endless shopping and nightlife options.
tips: Explore beyond the crossing - the backstreets of Nonbei Yokocho (Drunkard's Alley) and the streets toward Dogenzaka offer great bars and restaurants.

name: Shinjuku
description: Tokyo's busiest district with the world's busiest train station, the neon-drenched Kabukicho entertainment quarter, and Golden Gai's tiny atmospheric bars.
tips: Golden Gai (200+ tiny bars) is a must - some have cover charges for tourists. Omoide Yokocho (Piss Alley) has great yakitori.

name: Harajuku & Omotesando
description: Harajuku's Takeshita Street is the cradle of Japanese street fashion and kawaii culture, while Omotesando is Tokyo's Champs-Elysees with luxury architecture.
tips: Takeshita Street is packed on weekends. Cat Street (parallel) is more relaxed with vintage shops. Omotesando's side streets (ura-Hara) hide great boutiques.

name: Akihabara
description: Tokyo's legendary electronics and otaku district, packed with multi-floor anime shops, manga stores, retro game arcades, and maid cafes.
tips: Super Potato for retro games, Mandarake for manga/figures, and Radio Kaikan for everything. Try a maid cafe for the novelty.

name: Asakusa
description: Tokyo's most traditional neighborhood centered around Senso-ji temple, with old-school shopping streets, rickshaws, and a strong Edo-period atmosphere.
tips: Walk along the Sumida River for Skytree views. Hoppy Street has great cheap izakayas. Take a water bus from here to Odaiba.

name: Shimokitazawa
description: Tokyo's bohemian village with a maze of narrow streets filled with vintage clothing shops, independent cafes, live music venues, and small theaters.
tips: Best for vintage shopping and cafe-hopping. The area under the train tracks (Bonus Track / Shimokita Ekiue) has been redeveloped with cool shops.

name: Nakameguro
description: A trendy canal-side neighborhood known for its cherry blossom-lined Meguro River, independent boutiques, and some of Tokyo's best cafes and restaurants.
tips: Gorgeous in late March/early April for cherry blossoms. Starbucks Reserve Roastery here is stunning. Walk along the canal in either direction for great finds.

name: Yanaka
description: One of Tokyo's few neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing, preserving old wooden houses, narrow lanes, many temples, and a famous population of stray cats.
tips: Start at Yanaka Ginza shopping street and wander. The cemetery is atmospheric and historically significant. Look for cat-themed everything.

name: Koenji
description: Tokyo's counterculture hub with a strong punk and indie scene, excellent thrift stores, live music houses, and a down-to-earth local energy.
tips: Look Shotengai (covered arcade) has great vintage shops. Best explored on weekday afternoons for a relaxed vibe.

name: Daikanyama & T-Site
description: Tokyo's most upscale residential neighborhood with a European cafe vibe. Tsutaya T-Site is one of the world's most beautiful bookstores with stunning architectural design.
tips: T-Site's Anjin lounge upstairs is great for coffee with a curated vinyl and magazine collection. Walk to neighboring Nakameguro to combine trips.

name: Kichijoji & Inokashira Park
description: Consistently voted Tokyo's most livable neighborhood, anchored by the beautiful Inokashira Park with its swan boats and the Ghibli Museum nearby.
tips: Harmonika Yokocho (Harmonica Alley) has great tiny bars and restaurants. The park is lovely for a stroll and the weekend flea market is worth visiting.

name: Ikebukuro
description: A major hub rivaling Shibuya and Shinjuku, known as a center for anime and manga (especially for female fans) with Otome Road, Sunshine City, and huge entertainment complexes.
tips: Sunshine City has an aquarium, planetarium, and Pokemon Center. Otome Road (east side) is the female-otaku counterpart to Akihabara.

name: teamLab Borderless
nameJa: チームラボボーダレス
description: A massive immersive digital art museum where projections flow between rooms, responding to your presence. Relocated to Azabudai Hills in 2024.
tips: Book tickets online well in advance - sells out fast. Wear light-colored clothing for better projection effects. Allow at least 2 hours.

name: teamLab Planets
nameJa: チームラボプラネッツ
description: A barefoot immersive art experience where you wade through water, walk through flowing digital waterfalls, and lose yourself in infinite spaces.
tips: You will get wet up to your knees. Wear pants that roll up easily. Lockers provided for shoes and bags. Weekday mornings are least crowded.

name: Mori Art Museum
description: Contemporary art museum on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower, with rotating world-class exhibitions. Ticket includes the observation deck.
tips: The combo ticket with Tokyo City View rooftop Sky Deck is worth it for sunset. Late hours make it a great evening activity.
mapsQuery: Mori Art Museum Roppongi Hills Tokyo

name: Ghibli Museum
nameJa: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
description: A whimsical museum designed by Hayao Miyazaki featuring original artwork, short films, and immersive recreations from Studio Ghibli's beloved animated films.
tips: Tickets MUST be purchased in advance online and sell out months ahead - book as early as possible. No photos allowed inside. Combine with Inokashira Park.

name: Tokyo National Museum
description: Japan's oldest and largest museum with over 110,000 objects spanning Japanese art, samurai armor, ceramics, ukiyo-e prints, and Asian antiquities.
tips: The Honkan (main building) and Gallery of Horyuji Treasures are highlights. Friday/Saturday evenings are less crowded and atmospheric.

name: National Museum of Nature and Science
description: A comprehensive science museum with fascinating exhibits on Japanese natural history, dinosaur fossils, space exploration, and interactive science displays.
tips: The Japan Gallery focusing on the archipelago's unique ecology is more interesting than the Global Gallery. Great for a rainy day.
mapsQuery: National Museum of Nature and Science Ueno Tokyo

name: Nezu Museum
description: A stunning Kengo Kuma-designed museum housing Japanese and East Asian pre-modern art, with a breathtaking Japanese garden hidden behind the building.
tips: The garden alone is worth the visit - especially in spring and autumn. The NEZU CAFE overlooking the garden is perfect for a quiet break.

name: 21_21 Design Sight
description: A design gallery directed by Issey Miyake in a Tadao Ando-designed building. Hosts thoughtful exhibitions exploring the intersection of design and daily life.
tips: Check the current exhibition before visiting as it changes. Located in Tokyo Midtown's garden, nice to combine with a walk.

name: Mori Building Digital Art Museum
nameJa: 森ビル デジタルアートミュージアム
description: Another teamLab collaboration with Mori Building offering large-scale immersive digital art installations in a warehouse-like space on the Odaiba waterfront.
tips: Can be combined with Odaiba sightseeing. Similar to Borderless but with different installations. Check if still operating as teamLab venues shift locations.
mapsQuery: Mori Building Digital Art Museum Odaiba Tokyo

name: Intermediatheque
nameJa: インターメディアテク
description: A free museum inside the KITTE building combining University of Tokyo's academic collections with stunning contemporary display design. Skeletons, minerals, and scientific instruments in a gorgeous setting.
tips: One of Tokyo's best-kept secrets. In the KITTE building right next to Tokyo Station. The rooftop garden on the 6th floor has great station views too.

name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
description: One of Tokyo's largest and most beautiful parks blending Japanese, English, and French garden styles across 144 acres. A paradise for cherry blossoms in spring.
tips: No alcohol allowed. The greenhouse has tropical plants. In February, early plum blossoms (ume) are lovely. A perfect break from Shinjuku chaos.

name: Yoyogi Park
description: A sprawling public park next to Meiji Shrine where Tokyo's subcultures come to play - rockabilly dancers, cosplayers, musicians, and picnicking families on weekends.
tips: Best on Sundays when performers gather near the entrance. Adjacent to Meiji Shrine and Harajuku - easy to combine. Great for people-watching.

name: Ueno Park
description: Tokyo's most museum-dense park containing the National Museum, Science Museum, Zoo, and several art galleries, plus Shinobazu Pond and historic temples.
tips: Plan a full morning here to hit 2-3 museums. Ameyoko market street nearby is great for street food and bargain shopping.

name: Inokashira Park
description: A beloved park centered around a large pond with swan-shaped paddle boats, surrounded by cherry trees and connected to the Ghibli Museum.
tips: Legend says couples who ride the boats together will break up (local superstition). Weekend flea markets near the park are great for handmade goods.

name: Rikugien Garden
description: One of Tokyo's finest Edo-period strolling gardens, built in 1702, with a central pond, miniature hills representing famous scenes from Japanese poetry, and a lovely teahouse.
tips: Stunning in autumn for foliage and in spring for the weeping cherry tree illumination. Less touristy than other gardens. The teahouse serves matcha and wagashi.

name: Koishikawa Korakuen Garden
description: Tokyo's oldest garden (1629), built by a feudal lord with Chinese and Japanese design elements. The juxtaposition of ancient garden with Tokyo Dome next door is surreal.
tips: Beautiful plum blossoms in February, making it perfect for a winter visit. Less crowded than Rikugien. The full moon bridge (Engetsukyo) is the star feature.

name: Shibuya Sky
description: An open-air rooftop observation deck atop Shibuya Scramble Square at 229m, offering 360-degree views with a direct look down at the famous crossing.
tips: Book online to save money and skip lines. Sunset is prime time - book early. The open-air rooftop has a unique hammock area.

name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
description: Free observation decks on the 45th floor of the Shinjuku government building with panoramic views including Mt. Fuji on clear days.
tips: North tower has longer hours and a bar. Best for clear winter days to see Mt. Fuji. No reservation needed - just show up.
mapsQuery: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck

name: Mori Tower / Tokyo City View
description: Indoor and open-air rooftop observation decks atop the 52nd-53rd floors of Roppongi Hills, with unobstructed Tokyo Tower views. Often bundled with Mori Art Museum.
tips: The open-air Sky Deck is the highlight but closes in bad weather. Combo with Mori Art Museum for best value. Great for Tokyo Tower photos at night.
mapsQuery: Tokyo City View Roppongi Hills observation

name: Skytree Observation Decks
description: The highest observation point in Tokyo at 450m (Tembo Gallery), with a glass floor section and sprawling views of the entire Kanto plain.
tips: The Tembo Gallery (450m) is worth the extra cost for the glass floor corridor. Clear winter days offer the best Mt. Fuji visibility.

name: Tokyo Tower Main Deck
nameJa: 東京タワーメインデッキ
description: The 150m observation deck of Tokyo Tower with glass floor panels and a charming retro atmosphere that Skytree lacks.
tips: Less crowded than Skytree and has more character. The glass floor can be thrilling. The tower looks better from outside than the view from inside.

name: KITTE Rooftop Garden
description: A free rooftop garden atop the KITTE commercial building with a unique bird's-eye view directly over the Tokyo Station red-brick building and its Marunouchi side.
tips: Perfect for photographing Tokyo Station's beautiful Marunouchi facade from above. Combine with Intermediatheque museum in the same building.

name: Kamakura Day Trip
description: A coastal town and former samurai capital with the iconic Great Buddha (Kotoku-in), stunning bamboo forests at Hokoku-ji, dozens of temples, and a laid-back beach vibe.
tips: Use the Enoden tram to get between sights along the coast. Komachi-dori street has great food. Combine Hokoku-ji (bamboo) + Great Buddha + Hase-dera for a perfect day.
mapsQuery: Kamakura Great Buddha day trip from Tokyo

name: Hakone Day Trip
description: A hot spring resort town in the mountains with Mt. Fuji views, the Open Air Museum, Lake Ashi pirate ship cruises, volcanic Owakudani valley, and traditional ryokan.
tips: Get the Hakone Free Pass for unlimited transport on the loop route. Clear winter days have the best Fuji views. An overnight at an onsen ryokan is unforgettable.
mapsQuery: Hakone day trip from Tokyo hot springs

name: Nikko Day Trip
description: A UNESCO World Heritage mountain town with the spectacularly ornate Toshogu Shrine (the most lavishly decorated shrine in Japan) and beautiful surrounding nature.
tips: Buy the Tobu Nikko combo pass for discount rail + bus. The 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys carving is here. Shinkyo Bridge and Kegon Falls are highlights.
mapsQuery: Nikko Toshogu Shrine day trip from Tokyo

name: Omotesando Architecture Walk
description: A boulevard of luxury brand flagships each designed by world-renowned architects - Dior (SANAA), Tod's (Toyo Ito), Louis Vuitton (Jun Aoki), and more.
tips: Walk from Harajuku end to Omotesando crossing to see them all. Even if you don't shop, the architecture is world-class.

name: Prada Aoyama
description: A crystalline diamond-grid glass building designed by Herzog & de Meuron that's considered one of the most iconic retail buildings in the world.
tips: Best photographed at dusk when it glows from within. You can walk in and browse even if you're not buying. Right near the Nezu Museum.
mapsQuery: Prada Aoyama Tokyo Herzog de Meuron

name: Tokyo International Forum
description: A spectacular glass-and-steel atrium shaped like a ship's hull, designed by Rafael Vinoly. The soaring interior is one of Tokyo's great architectural spaces.
tips: The glass atrium (Hall A) is the star - walk the upper-level skywalks for dramatic photos. Free to walk through. Hosts an antique market on some Sundays.

name: National Art Center Tokyo
description: Japan's largest exhibition space designed by Kisho Kurokawa, featuring an undulating glass curtain wall facade. The building itself is the art, with no permanent collection.
tips: The Brasserie Paul Bocuse on the inverted-cone inside is stunning for lunch. Check what exhibitions are on. The wavy glass facade is best from outside.

name: Nakagin Capsule Tower Site
nameJa: 中銀カプセルタワー跡地
description: The site of Kisho Kurokawa's iconic 1972 Metabolism-movement capsule tower, now demolished. Some capsules were preserved and relocated to museums worldwide.
tips: The building was demolished in 2022, so only the site remains. Some preserved capsules can be seen at museums. A pilgrimage for architecture fans.
mapsQuery: Nakagin Capsule Tower site Ginza Tokyo

name: Shibuya Crossing from Above
nameJa: 渋谷スクランブル交差点（上から）
description: The best overhead angles of the world's busiest crossing, available from Shibuya Sky, the Tsutaya Starbucks 2nd floor, or Mag's Park rooftop.
tips: Starbucks gets packed - go early on a weekday. Shibuya Sky is best for wide shots. Mag's Park rooftop is a lesser-known free option.
mapsQuery: Shibuya Crossing view from above Starbucks

name: Tokyo Tower from Shiba Park
nameJa: 芝公園からの東京タワー
description: The classic postcard view of Tokyo Tower framed by Zojoji Temple and Shiba Park greenery. Arguably the most photogenic angle of the tower.
tips: Best at blue hour (just after sunset) when the tower lights up against a deep blue sky. Zojoji Temple in the foreground makes for a stunning composition.
mapsQuery: Shiba Park Tokyo Tower view Zojoji

name: Senso-ji at Dawn
description: Senso-ji temple grounds at dawn are nearly empty, offering a magical photo opportunity with the massive lantern, pagoda, and main hall without crowds.
tips: Arrive 30 minutes before sunrise. The Kaminarimon lantern is lit at night and turned off around dawn - catch it while still glowing.

name: Nakameguro Canal
description: The tree-lined Meguro River canal is stunning in any season but becomes world-famous during cherry blossom season when hundreds of trees create pink tunnels over the water.
tips: In February, the bare branches and quiet canal have their own moody charm. For cherry blossoms (late March), visit on a weekday to avoid massive crowds.

name: Shimokitazawa Backstreets
description: A maze of narrow lanes packed with vintage shops, tiny cafes, and colorful street art that perfectly captures Tokyo's indie-bohemian character.
tips: Wander without a plan - getting lost is the point. The streets around Bonus Track development are especially photogenic. Afternoon light is best.

name: Plum Blossom Viewing (Ume)
description: February is prime plum blossom season in Tokyo, with pink and white ume trees blooming weeks before cherry blossoms. A beautiful and less crowded alternative.
tips: Best spots: Koishikawa Korakuen, Hanegi Park (free), Yushima Tenjin shrine, and Shinjuku Gyoen. Peak is usually mid-to-late February.
mapsQuery: plum blossom ume viewing Tokyo February

name: Setsubun Festival
description: A lively February 3rd tradition where beans are thrown to drive out demons and welcome spring. Temples and shrines hold ceremonies with celebrity bean-throwers.
tips: Senso-ji, Zojoji, and Meiji Shrine hold major Setsubun events. The crowd shouts 'Oni wa soto! Fuku wa uchi!' (Demons out! Luck in!).
mapsQuery: Setsubun festival Tokyo temples bean throwing

name: Early Kawazu-zakura Cherry Blossoms
description: A special early-blooming cherry blossom variety that flowers from mid-February, weeks before the main sakura season. Deep pink and absolutely gorgeous.
tips: In Tokyo, find them along the Kawazu-zakura Promenade near Oshiage/Skytree, Yoyogi Park, and Rinshi no Mori Park. The blossoms are deeper pink than regular sakura.
mapsQuery: Kawazu-zakura early cherry blossoms Tokyo February
